subject: Request: annotated RBAC snapshot + SCIM delta for SIG review
messages:
From: Tim Collins <tim.collins@nebulahealth.com>

Cc: security-ops@nebulahealth.com
Date: 2026-06-17T14:23:00Z
Subject: Access artifacts we need for SIG (scoping)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nebula's InfoSec team has a SIG intake and they asked for a focused set of artifacts to close out the IAM section. Can you confirm if you can provide:

- A current RBAC export with owners annotated (who the role owners are)
- A SCIM delta covering the last 30 days (user create/modify/deprovision samples)
- A handful of SAML assertion samples that include timestamps and audiences

They'd like a short workback/timeline (2–3 business days preferred) and any notes on how least-privilege is enforced (role naming conventions, role approval flow).

We can accept redacted usernames if needed but they need the mappings and owner attestations.

Best,
Tim
Security Ops Manager
Nebula Health

Tim — thanks for the clear list. Looping Ben and Laura (IAM leads) to scope the export and confirm redaction approach. Quick answers up-front:

- RBAC export: yes — we can produce an annotated XLSX with role descriptions and an "owner" column. We typically include service accounts as a separate tab.
- SCIM delta: we can generate a CSV of deltas for 30 days; it will include timestamps and operation type (create/update/deactivate).
- SAML samples: we can provide 5 assertion snippets (redacted PII) showing NameID, Audience, and authnInstant.

Workback: target delivery in 48–72 hours. If Nebula needs full audit logs instead of samples, that will take longer and we should coordinate a secure transfer.

Action items:
- Ben to run RBAC export and add owner attestations.
- Laura to pull SCIM delta and include row-level operation codes.
- I'll assemble the SAML samples and write a short attestation note describing role naming and approval flow.

Is redaction of email addresses acceptable (we'll map to hashed IDs), or do you need true identifiers?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Tim — deliverables attached as discussed. Summary below and notes on redaction/controls: 

Attachments included:
- redwood_role_map_annotated.xlsx (contains: role_id, role_name, role_description, owner_name, owner_email_hashed, last_reviewed_date, environment_tag; service_accounts tab lists service account owners)
- scim_delta_20260615.csv (columns: timestamp, operation, user_id_hashed, attribute_changes)
- saml_assertion_samples.txt (5 snippets; PII redacted, authnInstant, Audience, AssertionID retained)

Controls & least-privilege notes:
- Role naming: roles are namespaced by environment (prod_, dev_, infra_) and by function (read_, write_, admin_). This helps automated linting during role creation.
- Approval flow: role creation/privilege escalation requires an approval ticket in Jira; approver must be listed in the owner column for that role and an automated Slack approval step records the approver.
- Delegated admin: delegated admin scopes are limited to sandbox and dev by default; production elevated roles require two approvers (owner + security manager).
- Service accounts: scoped narrowly with expiration where possible; where not feasible we use key rotation every 90 days and store credentials in our KMS-backed secret store.

If you need a CSV mapping owner names to hashed IDs (so you can reconcile), we can produce that in a separate secure transfer. For SIG submission we recommend the annotated XLSX plus SCIM samples and SAML snippets.

Next steps:
- Confirm receipt and if Nebula wants the owner-to-hash mapping file.
- If you need raw audit logs (session-level) we can initiate secure S3 share but please allow 5+ business days.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior IAM Engineer
Redwood Inference
